title: 26.8 · Three resistors in parallel
given: Resistors 1.60 Ω, 2.40 Ω and 4.80 Ω connect in parallel to an ideal 28.0 V battery.
find: Find equivalent resistance, branch currents, total current, branch voltages and powers.
check: Branch currents sum to 35.0 A and powers sum to VI = 980 W.

title: 26.21 · Brightness in series and parallel
given: Treat two bulbs as constant resistances 400 Ω and 800 Ω, supplied by 120 V.
find: For series and parallel, find currents, powers, total power and relative brightness.
answer: Series: 12 W total, 800 Ω brighter. Parallel: 54 W total, 400 Ω brighter.
check: 800 Ω is brighter in series; 400 Ω is brighter in parallel. Parallel gives greater combined output under the stated constant-resistance model.

title: 26.24 · Two ideal sources
given: Three branches connect top/bottom nodes: a 10.0 V source (+ on top), a 30.0 Ω resistor, and a 20.0 Ω resistor above a 5.00 V source (+ on top).
find: Find current through each resistor and the 10 V battery.
answer: 30 Ω: 0.333 A down; 20 Ω: 0.250 A down; 10 V source: 0.583 A up.
check: The smaller battery is being charged. Junction current is conserved: 0.583 = 0.333 + 0.250.

title: 26.28 · Three-branch circuit and node voltage
given: Top branch left→right: 2 Ω, 10 V source (+ left), point a, 3 Ω. Middle: 1 Ω, 5 V source (+ left), point b, 4 Ω. Bottom: 10 Ω.
find: Find branch currents and Vₐ − Vᵦ. Do only 26.28.

steps.title: Solve the junction equation
steps.math: I_t+I_m+I_b=0\\2(D-10)+2(D-5)+D=0\\5D=30\quad\Rightarrow\quad D=6.00\ \mathrm V\\I_t=(6-10)/5=-0.800\ \mathrm A\\I_m=(6-5)/5=0.200\ \mathrm A,\quad I_b=6/10=0.600\ \mathrm A

answer: Top 0.800 A right→left; middle 0.200 A and bottom 0.600 A left→right; Vab = −3.20 V.
note: Currents are positive from left to right. A negative top-branch current means 0.800 A flows from right to left.
check: Therefore Vab = −3.20 V. Both positive battery terminals are on the left; the polarity-reversal question 26.29 is excluded.

title: 25.59 · Supplement: tapered resistor
given: A truncated cone of height h has end radii r₁ and r₂ and uniform resistivity ρ. Current travels along its axis.
find: Find resistance using thin slices; check the cylinder limit.
check: When r₁ = r₂ = r, the limit is ρh/(πr²). This uses the thin-slice axial-current model requested by the problem.
